dct_title_s: Nepal Flood 2026 River Corridor, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli
dct_description_sm: OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the full Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridor in Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces, Nepal, for the 2026 flood response. The area of interest is a 1 km buffer around the river centrelines, running from Rasuwagadhi on the China border to the Narayani confluence at Devghat in Chitwan, across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahu and Chitawan. It merges the original partner shapefile for the upper reach with OCHA's HPCS corridor downstream. This is the wide planning view, the whole corridor under assessment rather than the ground that flooded. For data limited to the flooded area, use [Nepal Flood 2026 Flood Affected Area](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl), which clips every layer to the observed inundation footprint of 27 August 2026 and a 200 m margin around it. Every layer holds what is standing and what has been lost, so buildings and roads do not vanish from a download once mappers record them as destroyed. `status` says Standing, Damaged or Destroyed, and the Destroyed and Damaged Features layer gathers everything marked destroyed or damaged in one place. Layers are rebuilt straight from OpenStreetMap each day, so they carry volunteer work as it lands. Buildings, schools, health facilities and points of interest also come in an Overture version, which fuses Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap and reaches ground volunteers have not mapped yet. Overture follows its own release cycle and will not show mapping done during this response, so for damage work prefer the OpenStreetMap layers and use Overture where their coverage is thin. Subscribe to the dataset for updates as mapping progresses. - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/) - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)
